spec_match.rationale: Every trace shown is produced by a real Profiler on a page served with Document-Policy: js-profiling, and every number is derived from the returned object. The build's first framing — that the problem is samples with no stack — was corrected by measurement: across four deliberately different workloads, essentially every sample HAD a stack, and the failure mode is misattribution rather than absence. The index, the concept titles and the copy were rewritten to say what was measured.

interactive.rationale: A workload picker that profiles for a chosen duration and prints the trace, the leaf-frame distribution and the raw first samples; a four-workload comparison with pairwise verdicts; and a capability page that probes the constructor, demonstrates the policy requirement in a live srcdoc frame, and searches four traces for marker values.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index states the proposal's framing (gaps between stacks) and then says plainly what these pages measured instead, rather than repeating a description the demos contradict.

edge_cases.rationale: A browser without Profiler; a document without the policy (shown, not described); a trace with no attributable samples; a requested sample interval the browser does not honour, which the page reports by comparing sample count against elapsed time; and the distinction between an absent marker field and a null marker value, which the raw table prints differently.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5201297767792640 on the index and all three concept pages, with the WICG pull request that adds markers, the specification and MDN.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: Profiler exists; construction is refused without the document policy (proved in a frame that lacks it); a trace has samples, stacks, frames and resources; frames carry a name and a position; every sample carries a marker (the feature, expected to fail before it ships); and any marker present is drawn from the defined vocabulary.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 23 assertions. Measured: 300ms profiles yield roughly 30 samples against a requested 10ms interval; all four workloads produce the same two leaf frames with shares of 88–97%, and all six pairs are indistinguishable from their traces alone; 99 samples across four workloads carried no marker field at all; and an srcdoc frame without the policy fails with NotAllowedError: JS profiling is disabled by Document Policy.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the sample counts, attributable counts, distinct trace shapes and whether a marker field was present.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and the raw-sample and pair tables scroll inside their own containers.

accessibility.rationale: The self-time bars carry their numbers as text beside them rather than relying on length; the capability checks are text with an icon rather than colour alone; the policy frame has a title; every result is announced through aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Card and control grids are auto-fit minmax and stack at 360px; the bar rows use a minmax first column so long frame names wrap instead of pushing the track off-screen; tables scroll in their own containers.

openQuestions.title: Serve the whole feature under the policy, including the shared module
openQuestions.detail: routes/release.ts now sends Document-Policy: js-profiling for everything under this feature's path, which is what makes the demos work. Worth checking that the header is not needed anywhere else these pages reach — the shared workloads.js is under the same path and therefore covered, but a future concept that imports from outside it would silently lose the ability to profile.

openQuestions.title: Find a workload that produces stackless samples
openQuestions.detail: The proposal describes traces with gaps between stacks, and these four workloads produced at most one stackless sample in a 300ms run. Either the gaps come from a case none of these workloads reaches — a paint-heavy animation, a long idle period between profiled tasks, work in another agent — or Chrome attributes more aggressively than the proposal assumes. Establishing which would make the case for markers sharper, and would be a genuinely new measurement rather than a restatement.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible bar chart alternative for profiling self time
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not encode a quantity in bar length alone; give the value in text next to it and keep the whole thing readable when the bars are not.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each self-time row prints the sample count and percentage as text beside its track, and the same distribution is repeated as a string in the shape line on the comparison page.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts the shape strings contain percentages.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive comparison cards and wide tables without page overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Auto-fit grids with intrinsic minimums; wide tabular content in its own scroll container; long identifiers allowed to wrap.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Card grids use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(230px, 1fr)); the raw-sample and pair tables sit in overflow-x:auto wrappers; the bar name column is minmax(11ch, 22ch) with overflow-wrap:anywhere so a long function name wraps rather than widening the row.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

guidanceConsulted.query: sandboxed iframe srcdoc to demonstrate a document policy failure
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use srcdoc for a document that must not inherit the parent's response headers, and give the frame a title describing what it is for.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The policy demonstration is an srcdoc frame — it inherits no headers, so its constructor failure is caused by exactly the thing being demonstrated — and it reports its own result back by postMessage rather than the parent asserting what happened inside it.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: The frame reported NotAllowedError: JS profiling is disabled by Document Policy, in its own words.

summary: Three concepts built on real profiles, made possible by serving the feature's path with Document-Policy: js-profiling. The strongest result is one the build did not set out to find: four workloads chosen to stress completely different parts of the engine produce traces that are pairwise indistinguishable, which is a sharper argument for markers than the gaps the proposal describes — and it corrected the framing this feature was started with.
